exercise.name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Y Raise

reference.title: Dumbbell Bent over Y Raise (male)
reference.listing: Page not read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.bodyPart: Upper back and shoulders (lower and middle trapezius, rear and middle deltoid)
secondaryBodyParts: Low back and hips (holding the hinge)
exercise.mechanics: Isolation (shoulder flexion / scaption with scapular upward rotation)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the arms rise into the Y, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.load: Very light dumbbells (often 1-5 kg); the long lever makes them feel heavy
prescription.progression: Add reps and pauses before adding weight

cues.text: Feet hip width, knees soft, hinge at the hips until the trunk is nearly parallel to the floor with a flat back. Dumbbells hang under the shoulders, palms facing in.
Breathe out and raise the straight arms forward and out into a Y, in line with the trunk, thumbs turning up toward the ceiling.
Arms in line with the back, about 45 degrees out from the head; draw the shoulder blades down and back.
Lower slowly back under the shoulders; keep the trunk still.
Stay in the hinge, reset and repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears
mistakes.fix: Draw the shoulder blades down and back before you lift.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back to get the arms higher
mistakes.fix: Stop where the arms line up with the back; keep the ribs down.
Keep the arms long with a soft elbow.
Go light: the arm is a long lever at the top.

kinematics.norm: Nearly parallel to the floor, flat back (clinical opinion)
Arms raised in line with the trunk, about 45 degrees out from the head (a Y); prone raise above the head in line with the lower trapezius fibres gave the highest lower trapezius EMG (Ekstrom 2003)
Palms in at the bottom, thumbs up at the top (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #19371, Dumbbell Bent over Y Raise (male), video (movement reference only; page not read)
Ekstrom, Donatelli & Soderberg 2003, surface electromyographic analysis of exercises for the trapezius and serratus anterior muscles (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 33(5):247-258)
Reinold et al. 2007, electromyographic analysis of the supraspinatus and deltoid muscles during 3 common rehabilitation exercises (J Athl Train 42(4):464-469)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
The bent-over position loads the low back; keep the back flat and the weights light.
Raise only as high as you can without pinching at the top of the shoulder.
modify: Low-back discomfort: do it chest-supported on an incline bench.
Shoulder pinching: raise a little lower or use a smaller Y.
regressions: Chest-supported Y raise on an incline bench.
No dumbbells (thumbs-up Y with empty hands).

muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Pull the shoulder blades back and down to set the arms; the rig has no separate lower trapezius, which Ekstrom (2003) found most active in the overhead prone raise.

muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Upwardly rotates the shoulder blades as the arms go overhead.
